summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with left leg pain, swelling, and redness following a skin injury a week prior, concerning for cellulitis. She also had a mechanical fall resulting in a right shin laceration requiring sutures. She presented with URI symptoms, including cough, congestion, and wheezing, along with gastrointestinal symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Flu testing was negative, and chest imaging showed no pneumonia but mild pulmonary edema and atelectasis, consistent with an asthma exacerbation. Cellulitis was treated with antibiotics, and her symptoms improved. Her HCV viral load was undetectable, and HIV remained well-controlled. Anemia was noted, likely normocytic with borderline iron deficiency, to be evaluated outpatient. She was discharged home with services, on a 10-day course of clindamycin, with follow-up planned for wound care, anemia, and chronic condition management.
